This was a childhood favorite of mine and just as charming with the loveable graphics and the fun little puzzles like it was when I was a teen. Maybe that's where my fascination by fictional civilizations with strange technology and floating islands came from.

The minigames, location design, and perfunctory but unobtrusive story are actually pleasingly above average for this publishing category.

Unfortunately it is also an extremely short (~3 hours) game, even without skipping anything or abusing hints. This is despite the fact that it doesn't deviate from the lamentable formula endemic to this now tragically misnamed genre: a mishmash of unoriginal and ultimately optional "challenges" featuring mostly anything [i]but[/i] hidden objects, standing as superficial obstacles to trudging through an underwhelming sci-fi/fantasy story. 

Hundreds (thousands?) of these mostly indistinguishable digital dime novels have been published over the past twenty years, and being in the top half of this enormous and homogenous pile doesn't seem sufficient to recommend it.

Still, it isn't without its charm and I don't regret spending $3 and half an afternoon with it. If you have an unhealthy compulsion to play every game in this genre, you could certainly do much worse.

🧩 《Inbetween Land》简评：

这款游戏是一款由 Specialbit Studio 开发的解谜冒险游戏，讲述了主角寻找失踪好友 Mary 的故事。游戏以其独特的美术风格和谜题设计，为玩家提供了一段短暂但引人入胜的旅程。

优点：

视觉表现出色：游戏采用手绘风格的背景，营造出神秘而梦幻的氛围，增强了沉浸感。

谜题设计巧妙：游戏包含多种类型的谜题和隐藏物品场景，挑战玩家的观察力和逻辑思维。

多样的游戏模式：提供多种难度设置，适应不同玩家的需求。

缺点：

游戏时长较短：主线流程约为两小时，可能无法满足寻求长时间游戏体验的玩家。

剧情深度有限：故事展开较为平淡，缺乏足够的情感投入和角色发展。

互动性不足：游戏在互动元素上略显单调，可能影响玩家的参与感。

总体而言，《Inbetween Land》是一款视觉表现出色、谜题设计巧妙的解谜冒险游戏，适合喜欢探索和解谜的玩家。然而，其在游戏时长和剧情深度方面还有提升空间。

⭐⭐⭐（3/5）

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Inbetween Land is a point-and-click, hidden object adventure game, and seemingly one of Specialbit's earlier games. The artstyle of this game looks older and not as "fresh" compared to Stormhill Mystery and The Last Dream. However, I quite like it! It plays the same as the other 2 games, finding objects, combining fragmented ones, puzzles, etc to progress.

We play as an unnamed woman looking for her friend Mary, who's obsessed with a mysterious floating island above the city and one day disappeared after seemingly finding her way there. The island has beautiful, retro-steampunk-ish aesthetics which I really like. There are puzzles to solve as well, some of them quite difficult, but skippable if you don't care about achievements. Otherwise, just consult a guide or keep trying.

Two things I really like about this game and unavailable in the other 2 Specialbit games are the journal and the ability to "see" interactable objects. The journal shows what our character thinks while solving the mystery of the floating island, and the ability to see interactable objects highlights items with arrows showing that we can interact with it. This doesn't count as using a hint, so don't worry. However, there is no "fast travel" map so you might have to backtrack quite often if you're not careful.

My problem with this game is that it's too short and there are no bonus chapters. A short chapter about Mary discovering the island and getting trapped there would be nice. The notification for journal updates are also too subtle, and I forgot to read the last entries since this game is so gripping. Adding a complete, readable journal after finishing the game would be good, since after you finish it the game just resets itself and you will play from the beginning again. But it's still a very good, very cheap adventure game, so if you like these kind of games, no reason to not get it.

The puzzles carry it along!

This game by Specialbit is similar to their other games and is an HOG at heart, but there are very few HO scenes, and the ones that are there are more "find the pieces of a thing to do another thing in the scene" (find the pieces of the knife which cuts the curtain which uncovers the crystal and so forth) so there's a sense of accomplishment rather than just find a bunch of butterflies in a sci fi game.

The puzzles are well done and are just challenging enough to keep you guessing without having to take a hint or look up an answer, so again there's a sense of "I'm the little gamer that could!" at the end of the game.

The story is best ignored as it makes very little sense, but the graphics, puzzles and gameplay make this an enjoyable way to waste some time.

Look for a sale, but if this is your genre, this a a great addition.

Inbetween Land est une surprise pour moi, une bonne surprise... car le jeu est plutôt bon.

N'attendez pas de Inbetween Land une narration d'un Hidden classique car celle ci est plutôt mince et tiendrait sur un timbre poste coupé en deux ^^... 

Non, c'est plus sa construction qui m'a intéressé... Si d'abord on le considère comme un hidden, on se rend vite compte que son fonctionnement tient plus du point'n'click que de la première catégorie et bien qu'il y ait des SOC, ce n'est pas l'essence même du jeu mais plutôt de ses puzzles qui demandent un peu plus de réflexion que d'habitude...

Car oui côté puzzle, vous risquez de souffrir un peu... le jeu vous "donne" des indices à vous d'en comprendre le raisonnement... et y arriver donne une satisfaction personnelle que l'on a pas toujours dans les hidden moderne...

Côté graphisme, on retrouve celle des "vieux" point'n'click avec de l'infographie 3D où l'on intègre des cut scene et des personnages dessinés... le trait du dessinateur est agréable mais je trouve que le mélange des deux détonne un peu et "casse" le rendu final...

Le gameplay lui aussi à un côté old school avec une flèche que l'on doit cliquer pour faire un retour en arrière et une demande du jeu à mettre l'objet parfois au millimètre près qui parfois frise la crise de nerf.... On sait que c'est le bon objet, on sait qu'il va là mais pas à l'endroit que le jeu attend..... aaaaaaaaaaaaaaah

hum humm, maintenant que c'est dit... que penser de Inbetween Land? C'est un jeu avec une narration trop light à mon goût mais dont les graphismes sont agréables et les puzzles assez corsés pour retenir mon attention. Il vous faudra passer ce côté un peu austère du point'n'click pour y trouver le challenge et le plaisir d'avoir résolu les énigmes de cette île flottante...
